To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the crisis of human immunodeficency virus (HIV)-associated acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) and maternal mortality in the developing world is one of the greatest health challenges in the 21st century.

women are disproportionately affected by HIV/AIDS and pregnancy-associated complications in the developing world and that women have a fundamental right to comprehensive, high-quality health care, including treatment for HIV/AIDS, to avert pregnancy-related complications and death.

the HIV/AIDS pandemic and high maternal mortality rates continue to take a devastating toll on women worldwide and that governments and organizations have a responsibility to address these health challenges by providing woman-centered health services and by targeting resources to provide treatment for HIV/AIDS, including preventing mother-to-child transmission, and to avert maternal morbidity and mortality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What is the impact of AIDS treatment on pregnancy-related complications?
understanding the mechanisms that regulate the expression of the human immunodeficiency type 1 (HIV-1) and simian immunodeficiency virus type 1 (SIV-1) genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crisis of HIV/AIDS in resource-poor settings, particularly among women, is a public health emergency.
the health of women in developing countries is of paramount concern and must be addressed in a comprehensive manner.
the treatment of HIV/AIDS and the prevention of maternal death and morbidity in resource-poor settings should be a top priority for the international community.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are working with women in the community to provide them with the information and support they need to take care of themselves.
we need to provide treatment for HIV-positive women and prevent mother-to-child transmission.
the health of mothers and their children is a fundamental right.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the health of women and children in resource-poor settings is a global priority.
the HIV/AIDS pandemic has created a crisis of women's health.
we must continue to advocate for the rights of women and girls to health care, to reproductive choice, and to a life free from violence and discrimination.
